title: Buying a bass and playing with Kid Howard
summary: He buys a bass, is invited by Kid Howard to try it, and then plays with a big band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, guitar again by that time. And, uh, when, while I was up there is when I bought the bass. See, I always could play some on the bass, but I never did play jobs on the bass, see. So I did, I went, I bought a bass. So I had the bass about, I had the bass about 18 months. So this, uh, uh, boy just passed, uh, Howard, kid Howard? Yes. He said to me, he said, man, I heard you, you got a bass. I said, yes, but I can't play it. He said, oh, I know better than that. He said, I got to have a bass player. I said, I want you to play it. I said, well, if you can stand it, so can I. He said, well, I'll tell you what you do. He said, I have a little part at my house. He said, why don't you come on out with the bass? He said, I'll give you a chance to play it out a little bit. I said, all right, there's one center, you ran the next block and went on over there. And I played over there. And the fellas that, the fellas I played with, they never said one word about me playing the bass. It seemed like it was just something they already heard me playing.
About what year was that? Around 1940 or during the Depression?

Mm-hmm. So, right after that, I had played with Howard quite a while. And I played the bass with another boy named, uh, we always called him Don Raymond. See, I played with him and he had a big band, you see. Well, playing with him, it gave me a chance to get more acquainted with the bass because he did have music, you see. He used to play a lot of fun music, you see.
